en: A call roars like a peal of thunder,
like the clash of swords and the crash of waves:
To the Rhine, to the Rhine, to the German Rhine!
Who will be the river's guardian?
Dear Fatherland, you may rest easy,
firm and true stands the watch, the watch on the Rhine!
Through hundreds of thousands it flashes quickly,
and the eyes of all flash bright;
the German youth, pious and strong,
shields the holy border land.
He looks up into the meadows of heaven,
where heroes' spirits look down,
and swears with proud lust for battle:
“You, Rhine, stay German like my breast.”
“And though my heart break in death,
you will not become a Welshman for all that;
as rich as your flood is in water
is Germany indeed in heroes' blood.”
“As long as a drop of blood still glows,
a fist still draws the sword,
and an arm still cocks the rifle,
no enemy will set foot here on your shore.”
The oath rings out, the wave runs on,
the flags flutter high in the wind:
To the Rhine, to the Rhine, to the German Rhine!
We all will be guardians!
notes: stanza 2 is the refrain, sung after each of the other stanzas; the source gives it once.
line 3.1: 'zuckt es' = something flashes or jolts (a shudder, a flash of feeling) through them.
line 3.4: 'Landesmark' = the march, the border land of the country.
line 4.3: 'Kampfeslust' = eagerness for battle, delight in fighting.
line 5.3: 'ein Welscher' = a Welsh (Romance-speaking) foreigner, here a Frenchman; 'Welshman' keeps the old word's sense of 'foreigner' and is not the people of Wales.
line 6.3: 'die Büchse spannt' = cocks (draws back the lock of) the gun.
line 7.4: 'wollen ... sein' = want to be, will be.
